title: S&P 500 Hits Best Day Since August, Stock Futures Remain Steady – Live CNBC Updates
body:
U.S. equity futures slipped modestly on Tuesday morning after the S&P 500 logged its strongest single‑day gain since early August, a rally that was powered by a surge in artificial‑intelligence‑linked stocks, easing Treasury yields and a dip in oil prices. By 4:23 a.m. Eastern Time, S&P 500 futures were down 0.21%, while Nasdaq‑100 futures fell about 0.25%, indicating that the market’s exuberance may be tempering after the earlier burst of optimism.

The S&P 500’s August‑era surge was driven largely by heavyweight technology names that have been positioned as beneficiaries of the AI boom. Companies such as Nvidia, Microsoft and Alphabet posted double‑digit percentage gains in the previous session, lifting the broader index by more than 2 percent – the biggest one‑day jump in nearly three months. The rally also coincided with a modest decline in 10‑year Treasury yields, which slipped to 4.18 percent, and a 1.5 percent slide in crude oil, both of which helped improve risk sentiment across the board.

Analysts point to a confluence of factors that amplified the AI‑driven rally. First, the rollout of next‑generation chips and the expanding deployment of large‑language models have reinforced expectations that AI will become a core growth engine for the tech sector. Second, the Federal Reserve’s recent communication suggesting a slower pace of rate hikes has eased concerns about tightening financial conditions, allowing investors to re‑price risk assets more favorably. Finally, the decline in oil prices, prompted by weaker global demand forecasts and higher inventory builds, reduced inflationary pressures, further supporting the equity market’s upward trajectory.

Despite the upbeat momentum, market participants remain cautious about the sustainability of the AI‑centric surge. Critics argue that many AI‑related stocks are trading at lofty valuations that may not be justified by near‑term earnings, and that a correction could be triggered if earnings fail to meet lofty expectations. Moreover, the broader macro environment still bears uncertainties, including the trajectory of U.S. consumer spending, geopolitical tensions in Eastern Europe and the Middle East, and the potential for a more aggressive monetary policy stance should inflation prove stickier than anticipated.

In the futures market, the modest pullback suggests that investors are taking a “wait‑and‑see” approach, digesting the latest data before committing to further upside. The Dow Jones Industrial Average futures are marginally lower, while the Russell 2000, a barometer of small‑cap performance, is edging down 0.15 percent, hinting that the rally may be more concentrated in large‑cap tech names than across the broader market. Volume in AI‑related exchange‑traded funds has surged to multi‑year highs, underscoring the sector’s magnetic pull on capital, but also raising the specter of a rapid rotation if sentiment shifts.

Looking ahead, the next few trading days will be pivotal in determining whether the AI‑driven rally can extend beyond a single‑session spark. Key catalysts include upcoming earnings reports from major chipmakers and cloud providers, as well as the Federal Reserve’s policy meeting later this month, which could either cement the current easing narrative or reignite concerns over higher borrowing costs. For now, the market appears to be calibrating the balance between optimism over transformative AI technologies and the prudence demanded by lingering macro‑economic headwinds.
